source.title: From What to How: Attributing CLIP's Latent Components Reveals Unexpected Semantic Reliance
source.authors: Maximilian Dreyer; Lorenz Hufe; Jim Berend; Thomas Wiegand; S. Lapuschkin; W. Samek

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAEs to extract and analyze CLIP components, but does not test superposition or the claim versions about feature geometry, capacity, or canonical dictionary units.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on SAE-component interpretability and diversity, recorded below as related findings that fit no claim version. It does not measure feature overlap, pairwise direction geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. Its other attribution-faithfulness and robustness results do not test the claim. Toy Models of Superposition is cited, but cited findings are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study trains top-k SAEs on CLIP image-encoder class-token embeddings as a tool for its attribution framework. It reports SAE component clarity, concept diversity and attribution faithfulness. It never measures feature overlap or geometry, capacity competition, causes of polysemanticity, completeness or stability of SAE features, or feature dimensionality. The system is a CLIP vision encoder, not an LLM, so even the SAE-versus-neuron-basis concept count does not match V4 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate. The authors present SAE-plus-attribution-patching as a holistic framework revealing what CLIP components encode and how they drive predictions. It uncovers failure modes (polysemy, compound nouns, typography, spurious correlations) and a red-hue shortcut in melanoma detection. The low-clarity finding is a Section 5.2 result, not part of the conclusion. The final-layer focus is stated as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method; it uses post-hoc SAEs and attribution analysis on CLIP representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that attribution results depend on the reference samples used; this concerns attribution faithfulness, not the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP ViT encoders, most SAE components have low clarity, and clarity correlates with top activation (0.75). SAEs yield 5,363 unique labels versus fewer than 500 for PCA, and ViT-H/14 yields over 20% more concepts than ViT-B/16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on CLIP image embeddings recover more diverse concepts than the neuron basis or PCA, but many components have low clarity.

fits_no_version.finding: App. C: firing rate correlates positively with clarity. The authors say this contradicts the assumption that sparsity promotes interpretability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More frequently firing SAE components are not less interpretable in CLIP.

record.problems: The study focuses on final-block class-token embeddings and says this may miss earlier-layer dynamics. It does not assess feature-direction geometry or SAE-feature stability and completeness; the semantic alignment measure relies on Mobile-CLIP-S2, which the authors note may itself have spurious correlations or language ambiguity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted for the claim. Attribution-faithfulness and task-robustness results were not included because they do not measure the claim's subject.

record.verdict_notes: Toy Models of Superposition is cited only to motivate SAEs (neurons are polysemantic). No claim version is tested. The study's system (CLIP vision encoder) also falls outside V4's LLM scope.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested: overlapping or nearly orthogonal feature directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry in toy networks.
Not tested: whether capacity competition causes polysemantic neurons or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Not tested: alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
The study analyzes CLIP image encoders, not LLM representations; it does not measure features spread across LLM neurons.
The study evaluates SAE-component interpretability and diversity, but not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Not tested: whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Measured clarity of SAE components and filtered to components with at least 20 non-zero activations.
rows.value: The majority of components exhibit unexpectedly low clarity.
rows.note: The result concerns interpretability of CLIP SAE components, not the geometry or canonicality asserted by the claim versions.
rows.check: The row is correctly unlinked. The ≥20 non-zero activations filter is a selection criterion, not a result.

rows.subject: ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Measured the correlation between activation and interpretability.
rows.note: The paper says activation correlates strongly with interpretability; this does not test superposition geometry.
rows.check: The row is correctly unlinked. The 0.75 correlation is between top-activation magnitude and clarity, on the ImageNet-1k train set.
